value.title: Manali
value.summary: Manali is a city of about 11,000 people (2023) in Central Himachal Pradesh. A staging point for a number of treks (Beas Kund, Chandrakhani Pass) and sports such as white-water rafting, Manali is also on the road to Ladakh via the valley of Lahaul and Spiti and Rohtang Pass, which is the main attraction near Manali.
eat_highlights: Blue Elephant Cafe. It is a small eatery with good Indian and Western spread close to the bridge on the Beas River. You get the option of sitting and enjoying the food right next to the river gushing by. Try out the freshly made parathas, bruschettas, omelettes and traditional Indian tea.

Il Forno (ca. 100 m below the Hadimba Temple, in direction of New Manali), ☏ +91 98160 40144. Italian pizzas prepared by an Italian cook. Prices higher than Indian average but still cheap for Italian pizza.
transit_modes: There are various ways of getting around in Manali, if you are not already travelling with your own vehicle. Most tourists  hire a taxi (various kinds available), which takes you around to all the sightseeing spots in and around  Manali (Rohtang, Manikaran, etc.) It costs about ₹1800 per day, or a little over ₹3000 if you book together for 3 days (in the peak season). Dress for Rohtang costs around ₹150 for each set including boots and the ski set will cost you around ₹200. These details are mentioned on a board at Mall Road. Be sure to bargain.

Public transport is not so good. There are cheap bus services, but they are not so frequent. Yet, if you are going to stay for a long time, it is better to know the times and use them, as other modes of public transport and exorbitant compared to the bus. For e.g., auto rickshaws take ₹200 from Manali Mall Road to Solang Valley, while the bus will cost you just ₹10. The buses are not punctual especially because they seem not have a written schedule. The best option is to ask about timing at the bus terminal. Buses start to run at 7-8 AM. Frequently a bus can be cancelled or late. You can get in and out almost at any place on the route; just wave at the driver.
